vector_search_builder_workflow.overview: This workflow guides you through setting up and configuring the Milvus vector database for semantic search using local Hugging Face (sentence-transformers) embeddings.
vector_search_builder_workflow.workspace: This workspace already contains working code for this hands-on. Read it before generating new code, and follow it where it differs from the examples below. - setup/participant/.env holds the Milvus connection settings the instructor provided (MILVUS_HOST, MILVUS_PORT, MILVUS_USER, MILVUS_PASSWORD), EMBEDDING_MODEL, and COLLECTION_NAME. - setup/participant/common.py: connect_to_milvus() builds a MilvusClient from .env over http:// (the instructor's Milvus does not use TLS), and load_embedding_model() loads the sentence-transformers model named by EMBEDDING_MODEL. - setup/participant/schema.py: the product collection schema (product_name, price, category, description, and the vector field), its index (IVF_FLAT, COSINE, nlist 128), and the search settings (nprobe 10); the vector dimension comes from the embedding model. - setup/participant/insert_sample_data.py creates the collection and inserts the products from sample_products.py; setup/participant/app.py serves the /search API and the search screen. - Embeddings are computed locally with model.encode(texts, normalize_embeddings=True). - To check the API, use FastAPI's TestClient instead of starting app.py; the user starts app.py in their own terminal. - Run the participant scripts with the Python in setup/participant/venv, where requirements.txt is installed.

phase.ingestion_example:
from common import PARTICIPANT_LANGUAGE, connect_to_milvus, load_embedding_model from sample_products import get_sample_products from schema import VECTOR_FIELD, get_collection_name, product_text
client = connect_to_milvus() model = load_embedding_model() collection_name = get_collection_name() products = get_sample_products(PARTICIPANT_LANGUAGE)
# One row per product: the fields in schema.py and the embedding of product_text() vectors = model.encode([product_text(p) for p in products], normalize_embeddings=True) rows = [ { "product_name": p["product_name"], "price": p["price"], "category": p["category"], "description": p["description"], VECTOR_FIELD: vector, } for p, vector in zip(products, vectors.tolist()) ]
client.insert(collection_name=collection_name, data=rows) client.flush(collection_name=collection_name)

phase.milvus_search:
from schema import PRODUCT_OUTPUT_FIELDS, SEARCH_PARAMS, VECTOR_FIELD
def search_products(query: str, top_k: int = 5, filter_expr: str = ""): """Search the products, optionally narrowed by a filter expression"""
# Encode the query the same way as the products query_vector = model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True)[0].tolist()
results = client.search( collection_name=collection_name, data=[query_vector], anns_field=VECTOR_FIELD, search_params=SEARCH_PARAMS, # COSINE, nprobe 10 limit=top_k, filter=filter_expr, # e.g. 'category == "Camera"' output_fields=PRODUCT_OUTPUT_FIELDS )
# Each hit is {"id": ..., "distance": <COSINE score>, "entity": {field: value}} return [ {**hit["entity"], "score": hit["distance"]} for hit in results[0] ]

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app import app
# Entering the client runs the app's startup (model loading and the Milvus connection) # without starting a server; the user starts app.py in their own terminal with TestClient(app) as api: print(api.get("/health").json())
response = api.post("/search", json={"query": "red sneakers", "top_k": 3}) response.raise_for_status() for item in response.json()["results"]: print(item["product_name"], item["similarity_score"])
